title: Helluva Boss Season 3 Episode 2 Shows Millie Sparing Cass, Wrath Ring May Face Crimson and Andrealphus Threats
text:
In Helluva Boss Season 3 Episode 2, Millie revisits her past in the Wrath Ring, confronts trauma, and spares a nemesis in a duel. The episode hints at looming threats.
Helluva Boss Season 3 Episode 2, titled Bad Reputation, took viewers one ring down from I.M.P headquarters in Hell's Pride Ring to Millie's home ring of Wrath. The newly semi-secretly pregnant Millie joined her family, the Haymurders, at the annual hoedown of the neighboring farm-tool-and-weapon-manufacturing Wackford family. Music, dancing, brawling, and general festivities reaffirmed Millie's deep love for her family and her ring.
However, an encounter with an old nemesis brought up deep trauma. That trauma showed the audience Millie's deep and lingering guilt over the senseless deaths of a barnful of Wrath citizens. She believes she takes the blame for those deaths due to her own lack of skill and lack of action.
The confrontation begins when an angry imp named Cass interrupts the celebration. Cass accuses Millie of causing great harm to the Wrath community in the past. The scene then shifts to a flashback.
In the flashback, Millie and Cassidy were members of the same small team of assassins. They went after a notoriously hard-to-kill target hiding in the barn of the local Stiffwood family. Millie's then-boyfriend Chaz joined them after Cassidy pressured Millie to let him join the team.
Cassidy led a direct frontal attack despite Millie's objections that they knew nothing about the target's strategies. That lack of information had horrific consequences. The target, hiding among machinery in the back of the barn, activated a massive combine harvester-like machine with dozens of spinning blades.
The machine drove over the innocent farmhands as they scrambled futilely to avoid the blades. Millie, overwhelmed by the carnage and without her usual weapons, reacted too slowly. Multiple Stiffwoods and their employees were brutally killed in front of her.
Back in the present, the guilt clearly weighs heavily on Millie. Cassidy's accusations and taunts affect her deeply. Millie tries to walk away from the fight, but Cass slaps her with the Hoedown's designated Dueling Glove. That challenge forces her into a mandatory duel to the death.
The duel lets Millie's care for the people of her ring show through again. Millie insists on competing even when a loophole would allow her sister Sallie May to take her place. She soundly defeats Cass in combat and then spares the life of her old enemy.
Sparing a dueling partner goes against the rules of Wrath dueling, and her community looks on in consternation. Millie leaves the match satisfied, having settled her guilt over the lives lost. She defeated and then chose to spare the very person whose carelessness caused the slaughter.
The episode, which was heartwarming, heartbreaking and face-punchingly solid, placed emphasis on Millie's love for her ring and people early in Season 3. That placement sets the Wrath Ring up as a likely target for truly dangerous threats later in the season.
The list of Helluva Boss villains with reason to target Wrath grows by the episode. The first and most obvious is Moxxie's father, the mafia boss Crimson, from the Greed Ring. Crimson is a cruel and heartless imp who had a young Moxxie kill his own mother to show him the consequences of disobedience.
Crimson places loyalty to the Family above all else, and Moxxie was his sole heir. Crimson swore vengeance on Moxxie and Millie for Moxxie's abandonment of the Family. News that Millie and Moxxie are having a child will interest him.
As Crimson considers how to coerce Moxxie and Millie to hand over the child, he may find allies. One is Cass, who is humiliated but not dead and has connections to the Greed Ring through Chaz. Chaz had worked for Crimson himself in the past. Another is the recurring Wrathian villain Striker, who holds a grudge against I.M.P for interfering in his work.
There is one more possible threat to Wrath of a far more insidious and subtle nature. Andrealphus, the cruel ice-wielding Goetia demon, has taken Stolas' throne in his absence. A change in Goetia rulership may not seem to affect Wrath's farming folk, but Stolas had a vital annual duty in the Wrath Ring.
Every year at the Harvest Moon Festival, Stolas used his grimoire to let the light of Earth's moon reach the crops of Wrath, allowing for a bountiful harvest. That vital seasonal responsibility has now passed to an ice demon who is casually hateful to Imps at best and may actively seek to harm those around Stolas at worst.
If the ritual is not performed, Wrath's agriculture could suffer extreme damage. So could Hell, or Wrath at least, freeze over? Could Cass lead Crimson right to the Haymurders' doorstep? Or will Wrath remain the untouched, unbothered, eternally safe home ring that Millie cherishes?
Will I.M.P's most lethal fighter's soft spot for her home and family prove an enduring source of comfort, or a strategic weakness? For now, nobody can say. But the people of Wrath might want to get the harvest in early this year. Who knows what could be coming.
